newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ireland may be heading for hung parliament -poll.
newsitem.headline: Ireland may be heading for hung parliament -poll.

text.p: Irish Prime Minister John Bruton's "rainbow coalition" has dented an opposition alliance lead and the country seems to be heading for a hung parliament in a national election next Friday, an opinion poll suggested on Sunday.
The survey showed that between last Monday and Thursday Bruton's three party centre-left group halved an earlier eight point lead for the centre-right alliance.
His own Fine Gael party had gained three points to 29 per cent, its highest of the election campaign, according to the poll in Dublin's Sunday Independent newspaper.
The paper said that the poll "confirms that an inconclusive general election outcome is the most likely result" and that the role of a few Green Party and Independent MPs could be crucial.

The Sunday Independent/IMS poll found that combined support for the main Opposition Fianna Fail and the smaller Progressive Democrats stood at 46 per cent, four points more than the "rainbow" of Fine Gael, Labour and Democratic Left.
The poll, conducted on Thursday among 1,115 people, showed Fianna Fail, led by Bertie Ahern, as Ireland's most popular party with 40 percent backing.
A poll in the Irish Times on Saturday gave Fianna Fail and its Progressive Democrat allies 49 per cent, ten points ahead of the governing coalition.
Ireland uses the Single Transferable Vote electoral system which produces rough proportionality between votes casts for parties and seats won by them.
